metadata.title: ORJson performance improvements and benchmark updates part 2
metadata.author: crivetimihai

description:
Closes #1696

The remaining files all have valid reasons to keep json:

| Category                  | Files                                                                                                                         | Reason                              |
|---------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Protocol (needs strings)  | stdio_transport.py, wrapper.py, translate.py, reverse_proxy.py (both), main.py                                                | WebSocket/STDIO require string JSON |
| Human-readable (indent=2) | cli.py, cli_export_import.py, support_bundle_service.py, admin.py exports, create_jwt_token.py, request_logging_middleware.py | Pretty-printing for readability     |
| default=str handler       | pagination.py, version.py, db_query_logging.py                                                                                | orjson doesn't support default=str  |
| SQL functions             | sqlalchemy_modifier.py                                                                                                        | Database function arguments         |
| Database migrations       | alembic/versions/*.py                                                                                                         | Must remain stable                  |
| Special formatting        | encryption_service.py                                                                                                         | Specific structure requirements     |

The orjson conversion is now complete. All high-impact paths (SSE streaming, Redis pub/sub, request validation, tool invocation, config parsing, encryption, OAuth) have been converted.

**NOTE**: In sse_transport.py:
# Before:
json.dumps(message, default=lambda obj: (obj.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") if isinstance(obj, datetime) else TypeError(...)))

# After:
orjson.dumps(message, option=orjson.OPT_SERIALIZE_NUMPY).decode()

This changes datetime serialization format from %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S to ISO 8601 (2025-01-15T10:30:00).

  The MCP specification explicitly requires ISO 8601 format for datetime fields.

  | Format                | Example                   | MCP Compliant                            |
  |-----------------------|---------------------------|------------------------------------------|
  | Old (custom)          | 2025-01-15 10:30:00       | ❌ No (missing T separator, no timezone) |
  | New (orjson/ISO 8601) | 2025-01-15T10:30:00+00:00 | ✅ Yes                                   |

The previous code used strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") which produced non-compliant output. orjson's default datetime serialization produces proper ISO 8601, which is what MCP requires.

This is a bug fix, not just a change.

Sources:
- https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18
- https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2024-11-05/basic/
